answer: Interaction-graph random walks resist sybils: reputation propagates from a trusted seed set, and each hop needs a real edge another party actively maintains. To forge influence, an attacker must plant thousands of credible edges, but genuine interaction density stays sparse like a tundra, so fake nodes catch almost no walk mass and wither like a cut vine. Every planted edge risks being ignored by lazy peers, starving the walk and burying the sybil cluster in the cold.
